assertions.name: second_moment_exact_identities
assertions.source: ∫ s² dK_q = N^bal_q(3) = q^{−1/2}(1+q) = 2 + (√q−1)²/√q and d/dq N^bal(3) = (q−1)/(2q^{3/2}) — exact (sympy). For q > 1 the derivative is > 0, so on the family interval q ∈ (1, q₀] the second moment is monotone increasing with sup = N^bal_{q₀}(3) =: C₂ and inf → 2! = 2 as q → 1⁺: the uniform second-moment bound covering the WHOLE interval is exact and free (no numerics needed); the mass is N^bal(1) = 1 exactly (probability normalization, dK-framing = Attack A's A2 shift of the ds/s convention)

assertions.name: kernel_second_moments
assertions.source: ∫ s² dK = N^bal_q(3) for BOTH explicit kernels (atomic Jackson ⊛ theta via the separable Mellin factors [2]_p!·q^{1/2}; a.c. Jackson ⊛ log-normal via the exact Gaussian moment e^{2μ̂+2σ²} = q^{1/2}) at every sampled q (test, proton, muon, 1+1e-1, 1+1e-2, 1+1e-3), rel < 1e−30 (60 dps), and every value ≤ the exact monotone bound C₂ = max N^bal(3) = 2.00831604419 — the uniformly-bounded-second-moment hypothesis of the Lean tightness theorem is verified on the constructed family

assertions.name: markov_tail_bound
assertions.source: 0 = #violations of [K_q((R,∞)) ≤ N^bal_q(3)/R²] over q ∈ {test, proton, 1+1e-2, 1+1e-3}, R ∈ (2, 4, 8, 16, 32), BOTH kernel variants (atomic tail by exact prefix-sum over the separable Jackson × theta grid; a.c. tail as the Jackson mixture of log-normal erfc complementary CDFs; 60 dps). The observed tails are far below the Markov bound (exponential-type actual decay — diagnostic only; Markov + the uniform second moment already suffice for tightness)

assertions.name: uniform_tightness_certificate
assertions.source: 0 = #violations of [sup_q K_q((R(ε),∞)) ≤ ε] with R(ε) = √(C₂/ε), C₂ = 2.00831604419 (the exact monotone second-moment bound), ε ∈ {1e−2, 1e−4, 1e−6}, sup over every sampled q and BOTH variants: the single compact [0, R(ε)] catches mass ≥ 1 − ε of every family member simultaneously — the IsTightMeasureSet certificate realized numerically

assertions.name: second_moment_convergence
assertions.source: N^bal_q(3) − 2 = (√q−1)²/√q exactly (rel < 1e−30 vs the closed form) and strictly decreasing to 0 along q = 1+10^{−k}, k = 1..6 — the k = 2 moment-convergence hypothesis (Tendsto → 2!) that the Lean theorem isTightMeasureSet_of_tendsto_integral_sq converts into tightness via Tendsto.bddAbove_range + Markov

description: REP attack 2 — tightness of the balanced q-Borel kernel family (bean qou-ry7x, epic qou-q04o; audit-only, scope-(a), NO FIT, nothing wired). The explicit positive kernels with exactly the balanced moments (atomic Jackson ⊛ theta; a.c. Jackson ⊛ log-normal, σ² = ln(q)/2, μ̂ = −ln(q)/4; Attack B §3) form a q-indexed family whose SECOND moment is the exact monotone quantity N^bal_q(3) = q^{−1/2}(1+q) = 2 + (√q−1)²/√q — uniformly bounded on q ∈ (1, q₀] by C₂ = N^bal_{q₀}(3). Markov's inequality then yields uniform tail control K_q((R,∞)) ≤ C₂/R²: the family is TIGHT, verified here at 60 dps (tails of both variants vs the Markov bound at every sampled q; one compact window per ε catching 1−ε of every member). Consequence (carried in Lean, QOU/Archimedean/BalancedKernelTightness.lean): tight + [Prokhorov selection, Mathlib-gap class] ⇒ subsequential weak limits exist; + [moment passage, Mathlib-gap class] + the Lean-PROVED factorial determinacy pin (Carleman divergence + [CarlemanDeterminacyStieltjes]) ⇒ EVERY subsequential limit is the Schwinger measure e^{−s}ds — archimedean (REP) for the constructed family without fibre uniqueness (which fails: the fibre problem is indeterminate at q ≠ 1, Attack B §3.1). NOT closed: the identification of the substrate's own kernel with a member of this family (REP-1).
